proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(N=3n\).  By \(\text{def:projected-experiment}\), concatenation of \(D_K,D_D,D_A\) identifies \(Q_P\) with the law of \(N\) independent observations from \(P\).  Therefore every interval measurable in the three evaluation folds is an interval in the \(N\)-observation experiment.

First suppose that \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}=0\).  Let \(\nu_n,g_n^\circ,q_n^\circ,A\) be supplied by the first compatibility condition, let \(\eta,\zeta\) be independent standard Gaussian variables independent of \(X\sim\nu_n\), and put
\[
 T=g_n^\circ(X)+\eta,
 \qquad
 Y=q_n^\circ(X)+\vartheta_j\eta+A\zeta,
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\},
\]
where \(\vartheta_0=0\) and \(\vartheta_1=A\tau N^{-1/2}\), with \(\tau>0\) chosen below.  Taking
\[
 f_j(x)=q_n^\circ(x)-\vartheta_jg_n^\circ(x),
 \qquad
 \xi=A\zeta,
\]
gives \(Y=\vartheta_jT+f_j(X)+\xi\).  Centering and independence give
\[
 E_{P_j}[T\mid X]=g_n^\circ(X),
 \qquad
 E_{P_j}[Y\mid X]=q_n^\circ(X),
\]
as well as \(E_{P_j}[\xi\mid X,T]=0\), \(\eta\perp X\), and \(E_{P_j}[\eta^2]=1\).  Thus the law's \(g_0,q_0,\theta_0\) are respectively \(g_n^\circ,q_n^\circ,\vartheta_j\).  The first compatibility condition gives
\[
 \|g_n^\circ\|_\infty\le C_{\mathrm{env}},\quad
 \|q_n^\circ\|_\infty\le C_{\mathrm{env}},\quad
 \|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le C_{\mathrm{env}},\quad
 \|\xi\|_{\psi_2}=A\|G\|_{\psi_2}\le C_{\mathrm{env}},
\]
and
\[
 E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]=A^2\ge c_{\xi}.
\]
Because \(\vartheta_1=A\tau N^{-1/2}\), the coefficient bound \(|\vartheta_j|\le C_{\mathrm{env}}\) holds for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The two \(L^8(\nu_n)\) inequalities in the same condition show that the fixed supplied pair belongs to \(\mathcal H_n(P_j)\).  Thus both laws are in \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\), by \(\text{def:jms-law-class}\), \(\text{def:gaussian-branch}\), and \(\text{def:gaussian-nondegenerate-subclass}\).

Under \(P_0\), conditional Gaussian-density division gives the one-observation likelihood ratio of \(P_1\) relative to \(P_0\):
\[
 L=\exp\!\left\{
 \frac{\Delta\eta\{Y-q_n^\circ(X)\}}{A^2}
 -\frac{\Delta^2\eta^2}{2A^2}
 \right\},
 \qquad \Delta=\frac{A\tau}{\sqrt N}.
\]
Under \(P_0\), \(\{Y-q_n^\circ(X)\}/A=\zeta\) is standard Gaussian and independent of \(\eta\).  Its moment-generating function yields
\[
 E_0[L^2\mid\eta]=\exp(\Delta^2\eta^2/A^2),
 \qquad
 E_0L^2=(1-2\Delta^2/A^2)^{-1/2}.
\]
Independence of the \(N\) observations therefore gives
\[
 \chi^2(P_1^N,P_0^N)
 =\left(1-\frac{2\tau^2}{N}\right)^{-N/2}-1.
\]
Set \(\beta=(\alpha+1/2)/2\), so \(\alpha<\beta<1/2\).  Choose \(\tau>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), small enough that the last display is at most \(4(1-2\beta)^2\) for every sufficiently large \(N\).  Cauchy--Schwarz then implies
\[
 \|P_1^N-P_0^N\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(P_1^N,P_0^N)}
 \le1-2\beta.
\]
For every estimator \(\widehat\theta\), put \(A_j=\{|\widehat\theta-\vartheta_j|<|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|/2\}\).  The triangle inequality gives \(A_0\cap A_1=\varnothing\).  By the definition of total variation,
\[
 P_0^N(A_0)+P_1^N(A_1)
 \le P_0^N(A_0)+P_0^N(A_1)
 +\|P_1^N-P_0^N\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le1+\|P_1^N-P_0^N\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Taking complements therefore gives
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}P_j^N\!\left\{
 |\widehat\theta-\vartheta_j|
 \ge\frac{A\tau}{2\sqrt N}
 \right\}
 \ge\frac{1-\|P_1^N-P_0^N\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{2}
 \ge\beta.
\]
The interval is honest on these two laws because
\(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\subseteq\mathcal G_n\subseteq\mathcal U_n\).  Applying \(\text{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\) with radius \(A\tau/(2\sqrt N)\) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge \frac{A\tau(\beta-\alpha)}{\sqrt N}
 \ge c_0n^{-1/2},
\]
where the last inequality uses \(A^2\ge c_{\xi}\) and \(N=3n\).  Hence \(c_0\) depends only on \(\alpha\) and \(c_{\xi}\).  Since the nuisance product is zero, \(d_n^-=n^{-1/2}\), so this is the desired conclusion in the present case.

It remains to consider \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0\).  Put
\[
 a_n=\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}}{K},
 \qquad
 \widetilde b_n=\frac{\varepsilon_{q,n}}{K}.
\]
Because \(A\) is fixed and positive, the assumed product condition gives
\[
 a_n\frac{\widetilde b_n}{A}
 =o\!\left((\log N)^{-1/2}\right).
\]
Invoke \(\text{lem:jms-gaussian-fuzzy-support-benchmark}\) with sample size \(N\), exponent \(s=8\), treatment radius \(a_n\), source outcome radius \(\widetilde b_n/A=\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\), fixed source fits
\[
 \left(\widehat g\circ\iota_n,
 \frac{\widehat q\circ\iota_n}{A}\right),
\]
and \(\gamma=(1+\alpha)/2\).  Thus both the supplied outcome fit and its radius are divided by \(A\) before outcome rescaling.

For an arbitrary estimator \(\widehat\theta\) in the present experiment, define a source estimator by
\[
 \widehat\vartheta_R(W_1,\ldots,W_N)
 =A^{-1}\widehat\theta
 \bigl(\mathsf S_{A,n}(W_1),\ldots,\mathsf S_{A,n}(W_N)\bigr).
\]
The cited lemma supplies a bad law
\(R\in\mathfrak F_N(a_n,\widetilde b_n/A;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\), in the particular fuzzy support named there, such that
\[
 R^N\!\left\{
 |\widehat\vartheta_R-\vartheta(R)|
 \ge c_\gamma\left[
 N^{-1/2}+a_n\frac{\widetilde b_n}{A}
 \left\{\frac{\log(1/a_n)}{\log N}\right\}^{3}
 \right]
 \right\}\ge\gamma.
\]
Under the measurable transformation \(\mathsf S_{A,n}\), the treatment and outcome regressions become
\[
 g_{P_{R,n}}\circ\iota_n=g_R,
 \qquad
 q_{P_{R,n}}\circ\iota_n=Aq_R.
\]
Indeed, conditional expectation commutes with the bimeasurable covariate relabelling.  Substitution into the source equations gives
\[
 T'=g_R(X)+\eta_R
\]
and
\[
 Y'=A\vartheta(R)T'
 +(Af_R)(X)
 +A\xi_R.
\]
Thus the transformed coefficient is \(\theta(P_{R,n})=A\vartheta(R)\), the treatment disturbance remains \(\eta_R\), and the outcome disturbance is \(A\xi_R\).  The source support is Gaussian with unit treatment variance; independence of its treatment disturbance from its covariate and its conditional outcome-mean restriction are preserved by the displayed bimeasurable transformation.  Every remaining envelope, variance, and supplied-fit inequality needed for membership in \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and \(\mathcal H_n(P_{R,n})\) is exactly one of the second compatibility condition's displayed inequalities.  Therefore
\[
 P_{R,n}\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n},
 \qquad
 (\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P_{R,n}).
\]

The sample pushforward of \(R^N\) is \(Q_{P_{R,n}}\), and
\[
 |\widehat\theta-\theta(P_{R,n})|
 =A|\widehat\vartheta_R-\vartheta(R)|.
\]
Consequently the preceding bad-law inequality becomes
\[
 Q_{P_{R,n}}\!\left\{
 |\widehat\theta-\theta(P_{R,n})|
 \ge c_\gamma\left[
 An^{-1/2}/\sqrt3
 +\frac{1}{K^2}\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}
 \left\{\frac{\log(K/\varepsilon_{g,n})}{\log(3n)}\right\}^{3}
 \right]
 \right\}\ge\gamma.
\]
This calculation is where the order of operations matters: the cited theorem was applied with source supplied fit \((\widehat q\circ\iota_n)/A\) and source outcome radius \(\widetilde b_n/A=\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\), and only afterward did \(\mathsf S_{A,n}\) multiply the outcome, coefficient, and error by \(A\).

Let \(\ell_n=1\vee\log(1/\varepsilon_{g,n})\).  Since \(K=8e(1+C_{\mathrm{env}})\), \(0<\varepsilon_{g,n}\le C_{\mathrm{env}}\), and \(N=3n\),
\[
 \log(K/\varepsilon_{g,n})\ge\ell_n,
 \qquad
 \log(3n)\le c_1\log(en)
\]
for a universal \(c_1\).  Hence, by \(\text{def:rate-scales}\),
\[
 \left\{\frac{\log(K/\varepsilon_{g,n})}{\log(3n)}\right\}^{3}
 \ge c_1^{-3}\min\!\left\{1,
 \left(\frac{\ell_n}{\log(en)}\right)^3\right\}
 =c_1^{-3}\Lambda_n.
\]
Together with \(A\ge\sqrt{c_{\xi}}\), this shows that the radius in the preceding bad-law inequality is at least
\[
 c_2\left(n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\right)
 =c_2d_n^-,
\]
where \(c_2>0\) depends only on \(\alpha\), \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), and \(c_{\xi}\).  Apply \(\text{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\) to the embedded fuzzy support, with error probability \(\gamma>\alpha\).  Union honesty applies because this support is contained in \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\subseteq\mathcal U_n\).  We obtain
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge 2c_2(\gamma-\alpha)d_n^-,
\]
which is the desired conclusion in the positive-product case after renaming the constant.

Finally, \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\subseteq\mathcal G_n\) and \(\text{def:length-vector}\) imply \(L_G(C_n)\ge cd_n^-\).  The variance lower bound was used only to certify membership of the two Gaussian lower subexperiments; it is not used by the upper-frontier theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\) and \(1\le s\le\infty\).  For every sequence \(N\to\infty\), radii \(0<a_N<1\) and \(b_N>0\) satisfying \(a_Nb_N=o((\log N)^{-1/2})\), and arbitrary fixed supplied source fits \((\bar g_N,\bar q_N)\) that are uniformly bounded on the source covariate support, the recentered moment-matched Gaussian construction used to prove Theorem 3.2 of Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis supplies two fuzzy priors \(\Pi_{0,N}\) and \(\Pi_{1,N}\).  The lower-bound constant below is uniform over the recentering pair.  Let
\[
 \mathfrak F_N(a_N,b_N;\bar g_N,\bar q_N)
 =\operatorname{supp}(\Pi_{0,N})\cup
   \operatorname{supp}(\Pi_{1,N}).
\]
Every \(R\in\mathfrak F_N(a_N,b_N;\bar g_N,\bar q_N)\) satisfies
\[
 T=g_R(X)+\eta_R,\qquad
 Y=\vartheta(R)T+f_R(X)+\xi_R,
\]
\[
 \eta_R\sim\mathcal N(0,1),\qquad
 \eta_R\perp X,\qquad
 E_R[\xi_R\mid X,T]=0,
\]
and \(q_R(x)=E_R[Y\mid X=x]\).  Its treatment and outcome regressions satisfy
\[
 \|g_R-\bar g_N\|_{L^s(R_X)}\le a_N,
 \qquad
 \|q_R-\bar q_N\|_{L^s(R_X)}\le b_N.
\]
Moreover, there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of the estimator, such that for every estimator \(\widehat\vartheta\) based on the \(N\) observations there is a law \(R\in\mathfrak F_N(a_N,b_N;\bar g_N,\bar q_N)\) for which
\[
 R^N\!\left\{
 |\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta(R)|
 \ge c_\gamma\left[
 N^{-1/2}+a_Nb_N
 \left\{\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right\}^{3}
 \right]
 \right\}\ge\gamma.
\]
Thus the bad-law witness belongs to the displayed union of the supports of the particular fuzzy priors, rather than merely to an unspecified larger source class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix a sequence of supplied fits and radii.  Suppose that
\[
 \varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}
 =o\!\left(\{\log(en)\}^{-1/2}\right).
\]
Put \(K=8e(1+C_{\mathrm{env}})\) and \(N=3n\).  Assume the following two fit-compatibility conditions.

First, there is a constant \(A>0\), independent of \(n\), such that, for \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\),
\[
 \|G\|_{\psi_2}\le C_{\mathrm{env}},\qquad
 A\|G\|_{\psi_2}\le C_{\mathrm{env}},\qquad
 A^2\ge c_{\xi},
\]
and, for every sufficiently large \(n\) for which \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}=0\), there are a probability measure \(\nu_n\) on \(\mathcal X\) and measurable functions \(g_n^\circ,q_n^\circ:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
 \max\{\|g_n^\circ\|_\infty,\|q_n^\circ\|_\infty\}
 \le C_{\mathrm{env}},\qquad
 \|\widehat g-g_n^\circ\|_{L^8(\nu_n)}\le\varepsilon_{g,n},\qquad
 \|\widehat q-q_n^\circ\|_{L^8(\nu_n)}\le\varepsilon_{q,n}.
\]

Second, whenever \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0\), set
\[
 a_n=\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}}{K},\qquad
 \widetilde b_n=\frac{\varepsilon_{q,n}}{K}.
\]
There must exist a bimeasurable embedding \(\iota_n\) of the cited source covariate support into \(\mathcal X\) such that the fixed source fits
\[
 \bar g_n=\widehat g\circ\iota_n,
 \qquad
 \bar q_n=\frac{\widehat q\circ\iota_n}{A}
\]
satisfy
\[
 \sup_{n:\,\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0}
 \max\{\|\bar g_n\|_\infty,\|\bar q_n\|_\infty\}<\infty.
\]
Let \(\mathfrak F_N(a_n,\widetilde b_n/A;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\) be the particular fuzzy support in \(\text{lem:jms-gaussian-fuzzy-support-benchmark}\), invoked with these fits and source outcome radius \(\widetilde b_n/A\).  For
\[
 \mathsf S_{A,n}(x,t,y)=\bigl(\iota_n(x),t,Ay\bigr),
 \qquad
 P_{R,n}=R\circ\mathsf S_{A,n}^{-1},
\]
every \(R\in\mathfrak F_N(a_n,\widetilde b_n/A;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\) obeys
\[
 \max\!\left\{
 |A\vartheta(R)|,
 \|g_R\|_\infty,
 \|Aq_R\|_\infty,
 \|\eta_R\|_{\psi_2},
 A\|\xi_R\|_{\psi_2}
 \right\}\le C_{\mathrm{env}},
\]
\[
 A^2E_R[\xi_R^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}
 \quad R\text{-almost surely},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widehat g\circ\iota_n-g_R\|_{L^8(R_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{g,n},\qquad
 \|\widehat q\circ\iota_n-Aq_R\|_{L^8(R_X)}
 \le\varepsilon_{q,n}.
\]
Here \(g_R,q_R,\eta_R,\xi_R\), and \(\vartheta(R)\) denote the source law's treatment regression, outcome regression, treatment disturbance, outcome disturbance, and partially linear coefficient.  These displayed requirements are precisely the envelope, nondegeneracy, and supplied-fit compatibility conditions needed to embed the cited fuzzy support.  Uniform boundedness is required only after restricting the supplied fits to the embedded source covariate support; there is no global sup-norm restriction on \(\widehat g\) or \(\widehat q\), no small-fraction-of-\(C_{\mathrm{env}}\) restriction, and no requirement that \(\varepsilon_{g,n}+\varepsilon_{q,n}\to0\).

Then there is \(c>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), and \(c_{\xi}\), and there is \(n_0<\infty\), possibly depending on the compatible sequence, such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\), every evaluation-measurable interval \(C_n\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal U_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 Q_P\{\theta_0\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
also satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge c\left(n^{-1/2}+
 \varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\right)
 =cd_n^-.
\]
Consequently \(L_G(C_n)\ge cd_n^-\).  The conditional outcome-variance restriction is used only in this lower-bound subexperiment and is not a hypothesis of the upper-frontier theorem.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original universal fixed-fit claim can fail when the Gaussian lower subexperiment is empty or when the particular cited fuzzy support cannot be embedded within the primitive envelope and the supplied-fit radii. The proposed statement adds only the exact nonemptiness and support-embedding compatibility conditions used by the two lower experiments, plus the cited theorem's product regime. It removes the earlier global sup-norm restrictions on the supplied fits and the unnecessary requirement that the sum of nuisance radii vanish. The cited source is invoked with supplied outcome fit \(\widehat q/A\) and outcome radius \(\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\) before the outcome pushforward by \(A\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The former cited leaf stated a lower bound only over an unspecified larger source experiment and therefore did not ensure that the bad-law witness belonged to the support embedded by the proof. The replacement localizes the same cited lower bound to the union of the two fuzzy-prior supports used in the source proof.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorems 3.2 and 5.4 give a Gaussian DML lower bound and a fixed-positive-cumulant ACE point-estimation upper bound on separate classes.
proposed.matched_by: Theorem 5 under its explicit fit-compatible source-support embedding, and Open-ended Questions 7--9

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 characterize expected-length adaptation over unions in Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
The paper obtains composite-hypothesis lower bounds by moment-matched priors and chi-square control of normal mixtures.
Theorem 5 rules out second-order PLM orthogonality under Gaussian residuals, while Theorems 8--10 construct higher-order moments under non-Gaussian residuals.
Theorem 2 establishes coverage and interval-length control for the filtered union, while Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The JMS comparator remains an informing result, but its match must record that the present Gaussian-coordinate theorem uses it only through the explicitly compatible embedded fuzzy support.

prose_updates.tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). Under the exact fixed-fit compatibility needed by the relevant lower experiment---a nonempty Gaussian baseline on zero-product indices and an embedding of the particular JMS fuzzy support on positive-product indices---the certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\); outcome-noise nondegeneracy remains confined to that lower subexperiment. The proved contribution is the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier. The fuzzy-Hermite branchwise converse and removal of the Gaussian logarithm remain open-ended questions.

project_justification.gap: Published structure-agnostic PLM theory and the sibling repository paper study separate Gaussian or fixed-non-Gaussian point-estimation classes and fixed-separation spectral constructions, not one conditionally specified projected experiment with union honesty, shrinking cumulant separation, and branchwise expected length. The published Gaussian lower construction also does not by itself justify a bound for arbitrary fixed supplied fits unless its hard support embeds into the present envelope and radius set.
project_justification.niche: The informative object is the two-coordinate expected-length region; the global union supremum remains governed by the Gaussian coordinate on fit configurations admitting the certified Gaussian lower subexperiment.
project_justification.fill: The proved component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion for the shrinking-separation upper frontier. The Gaussian expected-length lower theorem is stated only under the compatibility needed in each regime: baseline nonemptiness when the nuisance product is zero and source-support embedding when it is positive. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is auxiliary to those lower subexperiments. The PLM-compatible fuzzy-Hermite converse remains open.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The statistical law class contains only primitive laws. The selected training-realized functions are external fixed inputs, and the upper theorem is uniform over all supplied pairs in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\). The Gaussian expected-length lower theorem additionally requires the applicable fixed-fit compatibility condition: the stated Gaussian baseline on zero-product indices or the fit-centered JMS fuzzy-support embedding on positive-product indices. These are lower-experiment compatibility conditions, not member properties of \(\mathcal P_n\).

prose_updates.related_work: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis, especially Theorems 3.2 and 5.4 and Appendices D and G, inform the Gaussian lower coordinate and fixed-separation ACE component but do not give a union-honest shrinking-cumulant interval. The Gaussian lower theorem here uses the particular fuzzy-prior support from their Section D only when a recentered, outcome-rescaled copy of that support satisfies the present primitive envelope and supplied-fit radii; the source outcome radius is divided by the scaling factor before pushforward. The auxiliary condition \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) is not attributed to their envelope and is used only for the Gaussian expected-length lower subexperiments. Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik, Theorems 5 and 8--10, inform the Gaussian obstruction and higher-order score. Cai and Low, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, inform branchwise expected length, while their Gaussian model has no learned PLM residual. Cai and Low's 2011 Hermite mixture method informs the fuzzy-prior handle. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman inform localized product-mixture calculations. Chernozhukov et al. supply the split DML benchmark. Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo's Theorem 2 informs filtered-union coverage and interval-length control, while their Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient; neither theorem uses treatment cumulants. The sibling repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\) proves fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions and explicitly leaves shrinking separation, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and a local matching lower bound unresolved. The present proved contribution is instead the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier; it does not claim a matching Pareto frontier. Quessy and Mailhot analyze centered and studentized normality statistics without nuisance-contaminated residuals. Armstrong, Kline, and Sun motivate caution about pretesting for a different point-risk object.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\), not \(d_n\). It applies to fixed-fit configurations admitting a nonempty Gaussian baseline when the nuisance product is zero and a fit-centered, outcome-rescaled embedding of the particular JMS fuzzy support when that product is positive; without the applicable compatibility condition the lower supremum may be empty, so no positive universal fixed-fit bound is possible. The source lower theorem requires \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}=o(\{\log(en)\}^{-1/2})\). Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy defines only the auxiliary lower subclass \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\). The upper theorem needs neither that variance restriction nor the lower theorem's embedding conditions and does not identify a matching Pareto boundary. Its finite-sample guarantee starts at \(n=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), when every requested calibration block count is available. The early kill test is a finite Rademacher-partition exponential-Hermite pair supported on primitive PLM laws, sharing admissible fixed supplied fits, and inducing projected mixtures with bounded chi-square distance and the target displacements in the open-ended question.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The law class is primitive and contains no learner-performance condition. All upper-frontier inference is conditional on fixed supplied fits and uniform over their radius set. The Appell polynomial estimates the first four raw residual moments on a fold independent of inversion. Every median-of-means operator partitions the sample into \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty blocks, and the upper theorem assumes \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\). Four named events receive error \(\alpha/4\) each, while the separate bound \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\) quantifies wrong-branch selection. The Gaussian expected-length converse is narrower: on zero-product indices the fixed fits must admit the displayed Gaussian baseline, while on positive-product indices they must admit the particular cited fuzzy support after fit centering, covariate embedding, and outcome rescaling; \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) is imposed only on those lower laws. The sibling repository paper settles fixed-separation spectral estimation, not this local-to-Gaussian union-honest length problem. The branchwise converse and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) are open. No matching Pareto boundary or unconditional improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: It records the Gaussian coordinate actually certified by the applicable nonempty fixed-fit subexperiment: the explicit Gaussian baseline on zero-product indices and the particular embedded fuzzy support from the published JMS construction on positive-product indices. It retains the published logarithmic factor and isolates conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy to the lower experiment.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem proves \(d_n^-\), not \(d_n\), only when the fixed fits meet the compatibility condition for the relevant nuisance-product regime. A universal lower bound over arbitrary supplied fits is false when the compatible lower class is empty, and removal of the Gaussian logarithm is not established.
statement_notes.consumer: On the stated compatible fixed-fit configurations, it prevents improvement of the global union-supremum expected length below the certified Gaussian scale.
